title: Booking Deposits Owed on Self-Pay Account In-Person Appointments
content:
## Rule

When the patient's financial account is on the Self-Pay Account tier on the booking date of an In-Person Appointments visit, a booking deposit is owed on the visit and the patient pays it by card as one deposit entry; a booking deposit not collected at booking stays owed while the visit is open, and it is worked out on the day it is paid.

| Record | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Patient Financial Account tier on the booking date | Self-Pay Account: a booking deposit is owed on the visit |
| Fee and deposit history of the visit | The booking deposit collected, as one deposit entry paid by card |
| Visit status | While the visit is open, a deposit not collected stays owed |

## The card payment tool

**Capability.** `pay_booking_deposit_d4a062b3` is the patient's own payment, by their own debit or credit card, of the booking deposit on one of their open in-person appointments. One deposit-collection entry paid by card, dated today and carrying the visit's encounter number, is added to the appointment's fee and deposit history, and the deposit shown as held on the appointment rises by the amount paid.

**Invocation.** This is a customer-side tool: it is unlocked and handed over to the patient, and the customer themselves runs `pay_booking_deposit_d4a062b3`; the agent does not run it on the patient's behalf.

**Parameters.**

- `appointment_id`: reference number of the patient's open in-person appointment the deposit secures, as the agent reads it out from the appointment list; an identifier.
- `amount`: the deposit amount the patient pays, in US dollars as a positive number with exactly 2 decimal places (cents), stored as given.

**Return.** A payment receipt with `appointment_event_id` (the payment receipt number), `appointment_id` (the visit secured), `payment_method` (always "card"), `amount` (the amount paid, USD with 2 decimal places) and `deposit_held_usd` (the deposit held on the visit after the payment, USD with 2 decimal places). The presence of `appointment_event_id` confirms the payment was taken; afterwards the patient sees the deposit held on the visit.
